section_summary: This section documents proceedings, political developments, and debates in the Imperial Japanese Diet between mid-1932 and early 1934, spanning the 62nd through the 65th sessions. Key topics include government policy toward the recognition and development of Manchoukuo, budget debates balancing agrarian relief against expanding army and navy appropriations, and controversies surrounding military involvement in domestic politics. The section also highlights diplomatic addresses by Foreign Ministers Yasuya Uchida and Koki Hirota, as well as an unexpected resurgence of Diet assertiveness in early 1934 challenging the military over international crisis rhetoric and naval treaty ratios.

subfiles.about: Extract of a Tokyo Embassy report on the accomplishments of the 62nd extraordinary Diet session, Viscount Saito's speeches, and General Araki's remarks.
subfiles.summary: Report on the June 1932 extraordinary Diet: three budget bills and nineteen measures; Saito regained confidence; Araki apologized for cadets' part in the May 15 assassination.

subfiles.about: Diplomatic analysis refuting Foreign Minister Count Uchida's Diet address regarding the creation of Manchukuo.

subfiles.title: Despatch Extract: Critique of Foreign Minister Uchida's Diet Speech on Manchuria

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 145 on the proceedings of the 63rd extraordinary Diet session.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Despatch No. 145: the extraordinary Diet session of August 22 to September 3, 1932 passed sixteen bills.

subfiles.about: Report section on the 63rd extraordinary Diet session detailing Seiyukai opposition, debates on rice control, and enacted legislation.

subfiles.about: Extract detailing the formal opening of the 64th Diet session and the party strength in the House of Representatives.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 278 on the reconvening of the 64th Diet session in January 1933.

subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Despatch No. 278 on the Reconvening of the 64th Diet Session

subfiles.about: Extract reviewing legislative proceedings during January 1933, including the fiscal year 1933-34 budget and electoral reform.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 278 extract: budget debate with critical questions on army and navy funds, a contested Electoral Law revision, and an Exchange Control Bill.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 278 (Extract): Proceedings of the 64th Diet Session in January 1933

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 314 on the subdued Diet proceedings during February 1933.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Political Report No. 63: the Diet met quietly in February 1933 with no significant legislation.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Despatch on Diet Proceedings During February 1933

subfiles.about: Extract reporting on mild Diet debates, budget approvals, exchange control legislation, and Rashin harbor development in February 1933.
subfiles.summary: February 1933: legislators avoided criticizing military appropriations; the Lower House passed the budget and an Exchange Control Law; Rashin harbor funding drew ice questions.
subfiles.title: Despatch (Extract): Course of Legislation in the Diet During February 1933

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 348 on the conclusion of the 64th Diet session in March 1933.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Despatch No. 348: the 64th Diet adjourned March 25, 1933 after twelve budget-related measures.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Despatch No. 348 on the Close of the 64th Diet Session

subfiles.about: Report on political inertia, cabinet stability under Premier Saito, and enacted legislation at the close of the 64th Diet session.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 348 extract: the quiet 64th Diet reflected fear of extremists; Saito and Takahashi stayed on; measures included disaster relief and an art preservation law.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 348 (Extract): Internal Politics and Legislation at the Close of the 64th Diet Session

subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum Forwarding Foreign Minister Hirota's Diet Address
subfiles.to: Secretary of State (Cordell Hull) and Under Secretary (William Phillips)

subfiles.about: Full text of Foreign Minister Hirota's address before the Diet outlining Japan's foreign policy and international relations.
subfiles.summary: Foreign Minister Hirota explains Japan's withdrawal from the League of Nations and reaffirms adherence to the Imperial Rescript promoting East Asian peace. He praises Manchoukuo's administrative consolidation and its impending transition to a monarchical regime under Pu Yi. Addressing relations with China, the Soviet Union, the United States, and Great Britain, Hirota advocates conciliation and diplomatic adjustment while expressing concern over worldwide trade barriers.
subfiles.title: Text of the Address of Foreign Minister Koki Hirota Before the Imperial Diet

subfiles.about: Cross-reference sheet for Despatch No. 636 on the convening and formal opening of the 65th Diet session.
subfiles.summary: Cross-reference to Despatch No. 636: the 65th Diet convened December 23, 1933 and adjourned until January 22, 1934.
subfiles.title: Cross-Reference Sheet: Despatch No. 636 on the Opening of the 65th Diet Session

subfiles.about: Extract analyzing the opening of the 65th Diet session, dissolution rumors, and anticipated political and economic controversies.
subfiles.summary: Despatch No. 636 extract: rumors of early dissolution discounted; expected issues were agrarian relief, trade controls, budget, May 15 sentencing disparities and peerage reform.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 636 (Extract): Opening of the 65th Diet and Anticipated Legislative Issues

subfiles.about: State Department memorandum analyzing Tokyo Despatch No. 673 and attached clippings on parliamentary attacks on the military.
subfiles.summary: Memo on Despatch No. 673: unexpectedly vigorous parliamentary opposition to the military in the 65th Diet, plus press on naval disarmament, the 1935-36 crisis and wheat anti-dumping.
subfiles.title: Division of Far Eastern Affairs Memorandum on Tokyo Despatch No. 673

subfiles.about: Report on the reconvened 65th Diet session, highlighting party cooperation in challenging the military over budgets and crisis rhetoric.
subfiles.summary: Ambassador Grew reports an extraordinary shift in parliamentary behavior as Seiyukai and Minseito legislators launched coordinated attacks on military dominance upon reconvening in January 1934. Interpellators assailed disproportionate defense spending, cuts to agricultural relief, and military warnings of an impending 1935-36 crisis. Navy Minister Osumi defended naval policy and warned the Minseito regarding London Naval Treaty responsibility, while Finance Minister Takahashi defended currency management and postponed tax increases.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 673: Resurgence of Parliamentary Assertiveness and Attacks on the Military in the 65th Diet

subfiles.about: Collection of newspaper clippings and editorial translations from the Japanese press covering Diet debates on defense, finance, and trade.
subfiles.summary: This enclosure compiles English-language newspaper clippings and vernacular editorial translations from the Japan Advertiser, Asahi, and Hochi published between January 26 and 31, 1934. The articles cover parliamentary clashes over military discipline, defense spending, naval treaty ratios, and public fatigue with crisis agitation. Additional clippings report on Finance Minister Takahashi's opposition to premature yen devaluation, Ministry of Agriculture plans for wheat import restrictions, and commentary on parliamentary revival.
subfiles.title: Enclosure No. 1 to Despatch No. 673: Newspaper Clippings on Diet Proceedings
